# Cleaning a dirty Excel sheet {#sec-clean}

```{r}
#| label: setup-clean
#| include: false
source("_common.R")
load_steps("code/1_clean_data.r", "clean")
```

| | |
|---|---|
| **Script** | `code/1_clean_data.r` |
| **In** | `data/fbs_mockup_trial.xlsx`, one row per patient |
| **Out** | `output/fbs_clean.rds`, one row per patient per visit |
| **How to run** | Step by step. Each step changes `df`, or `dfl` once the data are long. Re-run step 2 to start again. |

The sheet is a mock-up made for teaching. No real patient is involved.

## About the dirty sheet

One row per patient, with a date column and an FBS column for each visit at months 0, 3, 6, 9 and 12. Several staff typed it, and it shows their habits.

| Kind of dirt | Example typed in the sheet | Fixed in step |
|---|---|---|
| Patient number in many styles | `32`, `004`, `FBS-015` | 3 |
| Rows entered twice | the same patient on two rows | 4 |
| Many spellings of one group | `a`, `drug a`, `ยา a`, `group a` | 5, 6 |
| Many spellings of one sex | `1`, `M`, `male`, `ชาย` | 5, 7 |
| Units inside the cell | `62 ปี`, `27.3 kg/m2`, `5 yr` | 8 |
| Impossible values | age `999`, BMI `273` | 9 |
| mmol/L in the mg/dL column | `7.2` | 12 |
| Missing-value codes | `999`, `N/A`, `ไม่มา` | 1, 12 |
| Mixed date formats | `23 มิ.ย. 2568`, `45838`, `2025-06-30` | 13 |
| A mistyped year | a visit after the study closed | 13 |

## Step 1: packages, paths and lookups

To install a missing package, remove the `#` in front of the `install.packages()` line and run it once.

| Package | Its one job here |
|---|---|
| readxl [@R-readxl] | Read the Excel sheet |
| janitor [@R-janitor] | `clean_names()`, and turn Excel serial numbers into dates |
| readr [@R-readr] | `parse_number()`, the number out of text such as `62 ปี` |
| dplyr [@R-dplyr] | The verbs of the cleaning chain |
| tidyr [@R-tidyr] | `pivot_longer()`, one row per patient becomes one row per visit |
| stringr [@R-stringr] | Match the free text fields |
| lubridate [@R-lubridate] | Parse the dates |

The three lookups hold what I already know about the mess.

| Lookup | Holds | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `na_codes` | Text that means no value | `N/A`, `-`, `ไม่มา` (did not come) |
| `thai_month` | Thai month name to a month number | `23 มิ.ย. 2568` → `23/6/2568` |
| `study_close` | The day the study closed | No real visit falls after it |

The dots in the Thai month names are escaped. `str_replace_all()` reads the names as regular expressions, and a bare dot matches any character.

```{r}
#| label: clean-step-1
#| message: false
```

## Step 4: drop duplicate records

| Kind of duplicate | Rule |
|---|---|
| Identical in every field | Drop the copy |
| Same patient, one value typed differently | Keep the first row, and name the patient so the data collector can check the paper form |

```{r}
#| label: clean-step-4
```

`dup_id` holds `r length(dup_id)` `r ifelse(length(dup_id) == 1, "patient", "patients")`, id `r paste(dup_id, collapse = ", ")`. After this step `r nrow(df)` patients remain, one row each.

## Step 8: age, BMI and diabetes duration become numbers

`parse_number()` keeps the number and drops the unit.

| Typed | Becomes |
|---|---|
| `62 ปี` | 62 |
| `27.3 kg/m2` | 27.3 |
| `5 yr` | 5 |

```{r}
#| label: clean-step-8
```

## Step 9: impossible values

The patients are saved in `bad_baseline` first, so their ids stay on record after the values change.

| Variable | Rule | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Age | Outside 18 to 100 → missing | 999 is a missing code, and an adult trial has nobody aged 6 |
| BMI | Above 100 → divide by 10 | The decimal point was lost, so 273 was 27.3 |
| Diabetes duration | 99 or more → missing | 99 is a missing code |

```{r}
#| label: clean-step-9
```

`r nrow(bad_baseline)` patients have an impossible baseline value.

## Step 10: wide to long, and back

A mixed model needs one row per visit. The two functions are a pair, and each undoes the other.

```{mermaid}
%%| echo: false
flowchart LR
  W["<b>Wide</b>, one row per patient<br/>id · date_m0 · fbs_m0 · date_m3 · fbs_m3 · …"]
  L["<b>Long</b>, one row per visit<br/>id · month · date · fbs"]
  W -- "pivot_longer()<br/>fbs_m3 → fbs + month 3" --> L
  L -- "pivot_wider()<br/>fbs + month 3 → fbs_m3" --> W
```

| | `pivot_longer()` | `pivot_wider()` |
|---|---|---|
| Direction | Wide → long | Long → wide |
| Which columns move | `cols`, every `date_m*` and `fbs_m*` | `values_from = c(date, fbs)` |
| Column name | Split by `names_pattern` into `.value` + `month` | Built by `names_glue = "{.value}_m{month}"` |
| Result here | `dfl`, used from now on | `dfw`, a look only |
| Stata | `reshape long` | `reshape wide` |

`.value` means that part of the name becomes the column name, so `fbs_m3` lands in a column called `fbs`.

```{r}
#| label: clean-step-10
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
peek(dfl, 8)
```

`r nrow(dfl)` rows, which is `r dplyr::n_distinct(dfl$id)` patients × 5 planned visits. Going back, `dfw` has `r nrow(dfw)` rows again, one per patient.

```{r}
#| echo: false
peek(dfw, 4)
```

## Step 11: drop the visits that never happened

| Visit row | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| No date and no FBS | The patient stopped coming. Dropout, not dirt | Drop the row |
| Date or FBS present | The visit happened | Keep |

A mixed model uses the visits that did happen. It stays valid when dropout depends only on values we saw, which is missing at random (MAR).

```{r}
#| label: clean-step-11
```

`r nrow(dfl)` visits remain.

## Step 12: FBS becomes a number on one unit

The glucometer shows mmol/L and the lab reports mg/dL. Staff typed both into one column, so the size of the number tells the unit.

| Typed value | Read as | Action | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Below 30 | mmol/L | × 18 (1 mmol/L glucose = 18 mg/dL) | `7.2` → 130 |
| 30 to 600 | mg/dL | Keep | `126` → 126 |
| Above 600 | Missing code | Missing | `999` → NA |

The typed text is kept in `fbs_typed`, so every changed value can be listed with its id.

```{r}
#| label: clean-step-12
```

`r nrow(fbs_fixed)` values were converted or set to missing.

## Step 13: visit dates, one habit per line

Each line fixes one habit and leaves the text ready for the next line.

| Line | Habit | Typed | After the line |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Thai month name | `23 มิ.ย. 2568` | `23/6/2568` |
| 2 | Excel serial number, five digits | `45838` | `30/06/2025` |
| 3 | Buddhist Era year, above 2400 | `23/6/2568` | `23/6/2025` |
| 4 | Day first or year first | `23/6/2025`, `2025-06-23` | a date, via `dmy()` then `ymd()` |
| 5 | Visit after the study closed | a mistyped year | missing |

After the step, look at `date` and `txt` side by side. That comparison is the whole lesson. A date still missing here had something typed in the sheet, so the step names those rows for the data collector and keeps them.

```{r}
#| label: clean-step-13
```

`r nrow(date_bad)` visit `r ifelse(nrow(date_bad) == 1, "date", "dates")` could not be used.

## Step 14: time since the first visit

Month 3 is the plan. The real visit can be a few days early or late.

| New column | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `days` | Actual days since the month 0 visit |
| `time_months` | Actual calendar months since month 0. Falls back to the planned month when the date is missing |
| due date | Month 0 date + planned months |

| Detail | Example |
|---|---|
| lubridate counts real calendar months | 15 Jan → 15 Apr = exactly 3 |
| `%m+%` stays inside the month | 31 Jan + 1 month = 28 or 29 Feb, not March |
| Write `period(month = month)` | `period(month, units = "months")` adds the whole column into one period, so every visit gets the same due date |

Visits more than 3 weeks from their due date go into `off_window` for a look.

```{r}
#| label: clean-step-14
```

`off_window` holds `r nrow(off_window)` visits.

## Step 16: check

The script stops if a cleaned number does not match what is known for this dataset. A wrong cleaning rule would break one of these.

| Check | Expected |
|---|---|
| Patients and visits | The known totals |
| Month 0 visit | Every patient has one |
| Duplicate visits | None |
| Months | Only 0, 3, 6, 9, 12 |
| Treatment | No missing |
| Sex | Two levels |
| FBS | 40 to 400 mg/dL |
| Days since month 0 | Never negative |

```{r}
#| label: clean-step-16
```

The cleaned data hold `r dplyr::n_distinct(dfl$id)` patients and `r nrow(dfl)` visits.
